parentalite.q1: Why do you want a child?
parentalite.q1a: Because we both deeply want one, we've been talking about it for a long time and it's a well-thought-out decision.
parentalite.q1b: The desire is there, but it's mostly one of us pushing while the other goes along.
parentalite.q1c: Our parents are pressuring us, all our friends have kids, so we figure it's time.
parentalite.q1d: We're hoping it will bring us closer or give our relationship new meaning.
parentalite.q2: Are you ready to wake up every night for 2 to 3 years?
parentalite.q2a: We know it's going to be tough. We've talked about it and even planned how to take turns.
parentalite.q2b: We expect the nights will be rough, but we'll figure it out as we go.
parentalite.q2c: Meh, babies eventually learn to sleep, right? It can't last that long.
parentalite.q3: Could your current financial situation handle an extra $500 to $800 in monthly expenses?
parentalite.q3a: Yes, we have savings and our income comfortably covers that extra cost.
parentalite.q3b: It would be tight, but doable with some adjustments.
parentalite.q3c: Honestly, we're already struggling to make ends meet.
parentalite.q4: How do you handle conflicts in your relationship today?
parentalite.q4a: We talk it out, even when it's tense. We always end up finding common ground.
parentalite.q4b: It depends on the topic. On some things, we get stuck and let it drag on.
parentalite.q4c: We either fight or give each other the silent treatment. Then it blows over.
parentalite.q5: Have you discussed your parenting values together?
parentalite.q5a: Yes, in depth. We know where we agree and where we'll need to compromise.
parentalite.q5b: Vaguely. We've touched on the topic without going into detail.
parentalite.q5c: Not really, we'll figure it out when the time comes.
parentalite.q6: Who will take care of the baby day-to-day? Have you discussed this concretely?
parentalite.q6a: We have a clear plan: parental leave, shift arrangements, nighttime and task responsibilities.
parentalite.q6b: We know it'll be a shared effort, but we haven't worked out the details yet.
parentalite.q6c: We haven't discussed it. It'll work itself out naturally.
parentalite.q7: How do you react to extreme stress and exhaustion?
parentalite.q7a: I get irritable, but I'm aware of it and I adjust.
parentalite.q7b: I withdraw into myself. It's not great, but I'm conscious of it.
parentalite.q7c: I lose it. Exhaustion is really not my thing.
parentalite.q8: Is your relationship going through a stable period right now?
parentalite.q8a: Yes, we're in a good place. Solid.
parentalite.q8b: Some tension, but nothing serious. Just a minor rough patch.
parentalite.q8c: It's complicated. We're not even sure it's going to last.
parentalite.q9: Are you ready to put your social life on hold for at least 1 to 2 years?
parentalite.q9a: Yes, I've already made peace with saying goodbye to spontaneous nights out and lazy mornings.
parentalite.q9b: I know things will change, but I hope to keep at least some social life.
parentalite.q9c: Uh... no. I'm not ready to give that up.
parentalite.q10: How do you currently split household chores?
parentalite.q10a: It's fairly balanced, each of us does their share without being asked.
parentalite.q10b: One of us does more than the other, but we talk about it.
parentalite.q10c: It's unbalanced and it's a recurring source of tension.
parentalite.q11: Do you have suitable housing (or housing that could be adapted) for a child?
parentalite.q11a: Yes, we have enough space and stability.
parentalite.q11b: Not ideal, but we have a plan to move or make adjustments.
parentalite.q11c: We're in a tiny apartment with no prospect of change anytime soon.
parentalite.q12: Your relationship with your own parents: what impact does it have on your desire for a child?
parentalite.q12a: I've made peace with my childhood (good or difficult). I know what kind of parent I want to be.
parentalite.q12b: There are unresolved things, but I'm working on them.
parentalite.q12c: I'm afraid of repeating my parents' mistakes. It holds me back.
parentalite.q13: Is your professional situation compatible with having a child?
parentalite.q13a: Yes: permanent job or stable income, leave available, understanding employer.
parentalite.q13b: It's manageable, but we'd have to juggle a bit.
parentalite.q13c: It's a total blur career-wise. Having a child now would be a leap into the unknown.
parentalite.q14: Do you have a support network around you (family, close friends)?
parentalite.q14a: Yes, reliable and available people who can help us.
parentalite.q14b: A few people, but not necessarily nearby.
parentalite.q14c: No, we'd be truly on our own in this.
parentalite.q15: If you found out tomorrow that you're expecting a child, what would your honest first reaction be?
parentalite.q15a: Immense joy, even if a little scary.
parentalite.q15b: Surprise, a mix of excitement and anxiety.
parentalite.q15c: Panic. We're not ready at all.
parentalite.q16: Do you agree on the number of children you want?
parentalite.q16a: Yes, we've discussed it and we're aligned.
parentalite.q16b: Not exactly, but we're open to discussion.
parentalite.q16c: We've never talked about it, or we completely disagree.
parentalite.q17: How do you feel around other people's children?
parentalite.q17a: I love it. Even when it's noisy and chaotic, it makes me smile.
parentalite.q17b: It depends. An hour is fine, a whole day is exhausting.
parentalite.q17c: I can't stand the crying, screaming, and mess. It stresses me out deeply.
parentalite.q18: Do you have important personal projects that would be incompatible with a baby?
parentalite.q18a: No, or they're projects we can adapt. The timing is right.
parentalite.q18b: Yes, but I'm ready to postpone or slow them down.
parentalite.q18c: Yes, and giving them up now would make me unhappy.
parentalite.q19: Are you aware that your relationship will be put to the test?
parentalite.q19a: Yes. We know the first months will be intense. We've talked about how to support each other.
parentalite.q19b: We suspect so, but we don't really have a plan.
parentalite.q19c: A child brings you closer together. We don't see the problem.
parentalite.q20: Being 100% honest with yourself: do you truly feel ready to become a parent?
parentalite.q20a: Yes. Not perfectly ready (nobody is), but ready to try, to learn, to commit.
parentalite.q20b: I'm still hesitating. The desire is there, but something holds me back.
parentalite.q20c: No. And deep down, I think I know it.
parentalite.r1_t: There's a long way to go, take your time
parentalite.r1_d: This score isn't a judgment. It's a signal. It indicates that many things need to be addressed before even considering a child. Your relationship, your personal situation, your fears, your finances... all of this needs attention. A child doesn't fix anything. It amplifies what's already there.
parentalite.r1_a: Before thinking 'baby,' think 'couple.' Is your relationship healthy? Solid? Fulfilling? If the answer makes you hesitate, that's where you should focus your energy.
parentalite.r2_t: Not the right time yet, and that's OK
parentalite.r2_d: Your score reflects some significant blind spots. That doesn't mean you'll never be ready. It means that today, certain conditions aren't met. And recognizing that is already a sign of maturity.
parentalite.r2_a: Identify the 2-3 most critical points (finances? relationship stability? agreement on the project?) and actively work on them.
parentalite.r3_t: Almost ready, a few areas to strengthen
parentalite.r3_d: The desire is there, and so is the foundation of your relationship. But some topics remain unclear or haven't been discussed between you yet. Finances, division of responsibilities, parenting vision... there are conversations to have before taking the leap.
parentalite.r3_a: Go back to the questions where you scored lowest and make them a real discussion topic, on a calm evening when you're both feeling good.
parentalite.r4_t: You're ready (or very close to it)
parentalite.r4_d: Your answers show a couple that has done the groundwork. You've discussed the topics that matter, you know your strengths and vulnerabilities, and you're approaching parenthood with clear-eyed realism.
parentalite.r4_a: Go for it. Keep communicating, maintain that honesty with each other. Doubting sometimes doesn't mean you're not ready. It's actually a good sign.
